parts.name: frame body

physics.Basic_description: The main C-shaped body of the clamp, painted bright orange with a matte finish, appearing robust and heavy.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural backbone that resists the clamping force and holds the screw mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the top or side of the C-frame firmly to stabilize the tool during operation.
physics.reason: Small hand tool frames are typically solid cast metal to withstand high clamping forces without bending.

parts.description: The main C-shaped body of the clamp, painted bright orange with a matte finish, appearing robust and heavy.
parts.function: Provides the structural backbone that resists the clamping force and holds the screw mechanism.

parts.name: anvil pad

physics.Basic_description: A small, flat, silver-colored circular pad located on the inner jaw of the frame.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a hard, flat surface for the workpiece to rest against while being clamped.
physics.Grasped_description: Not intended for grasping; it is a contact surface for the workpiece.
physics.reason: Small wear pad designed to transmit force directly.

parts.description: A small, flat, silver-colored circular pad located on the inner jaw of the frame.
parts.function: Provides a hard, flat surface for the workpiece to rest against while being clamped.

parts.name: screw core

physics.Basic_description: The threaded silver metal rod running through the center of the clamp mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Converts rotational motion from the handle into linear clamping force.
physics.Grasped_description: Avoid grasping the threads directly as it may damage them or slip; grasp the handle instead.
physics.reason: Standard threaded rod construction is solid steel.

parts.description: The threaded silver metal rod running through the center of the clamp mechanism.
parts.function: Converts rotational motion from the handle into linear clamping force.

parts.name: screw collar

physics.Basic_description: A silver cylindrical collar or nut housing at the end of the screw assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the screw mechanism within the frame and allows rotation.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integral to the mechanism to be a primary grasp point.
physics.reason: Likely a machined solid component or thick-walled bushing.

parts.description: A silver cylindrical collar or nut housing at the end of the screw assembly.
parts.function: Secures the screw mechanism within the frame and allows rotation.

parts.name: lever hub

physics.Basic_description: The orange painted central hub connecting the handle arm to the screw head.
physics.Functional_description: Transfers torque from the handle to the screw.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to rotate the screw if the handle is inaccessible, though less ergonomic.
physics.reason: Cast metal component designed to handle torsional stress.

parts.description: The orange painted central hub connecting the handle arm to the screw head.
parts.function: Transfers torque from the handle to the screw.

parts.name: lever arm

physics.Basic_description: The orange painted rod extending upwards from the hub, serving as the lever arm.
physics.Functional_description: Provides leverage distance for the user to apply torque to the screw.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the middle of the arm to rotate the clamp mechanism.
physics.reason: Lever arms require rigidity and are typically solid rods.

parts.description: The orange painted rod extending upwards from the hub, serving as the lever arm.
parts.function: Provides leverage distance for the user to apply torque to the screw.

parts.name: lever grip

physics.Basic_description: The black, ribbed cylindrical grip at the top of the handle.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a comfortable, high-friction surface for the user's hand to turn the clamp.
physics.Grasped_description: Primary grasp point; pinch or wrap around the cylinder to rotate the screw.
physics.reason: Molded rubber grip is effectively solid for manipulation purposes.

parts.description: The black, ribbed cylindrical grip at the top of the handle.

parts.name: grip ridge 0

physics.Basic_description: The textured ridges on the black handle grip.
physics.Functional_description: Increases friction to prevent the hand or gripper from slipping during rotation.
physics.Grasped_description: The ridges enhance the grip security when grasping the handle.
physics.reason: Surface feature of the solid rubber grip.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
